# The Story So Far {#story}

#### *A Road Made of Salt*

Long before the canals, a pale road of packed salt crossed the Anvil Basin from the mining town of Ashgate to the sea gate at Gullhaven. Seven towns grew along it. Now the old trading houses are gone, the Merchants' Guild has reopened the road for one more season, and every house with a wagon and a little coin wants the best of the trade.

#### *Coin Is Not Enough*

Having the most gold at the end is not the same as winning. Permits decide who may travel, contracts decide who gets paid twice, and the Guild decides who is trusted. Learn when to bid high, when to wait in town, and when to take the longer road to avoid a toll.

#### *Mind The Rumors*

Every round a Rumor card whispers about shortages, festivals, and closed gates. Rumors move prices. A house that reads them early will buy low and sell high.

# How The Game Works {#how}

Saltroad is a trading game for two to five houses. Each house runs a single wagon back and forth along the Salt Road for **eight rounds**, which together make up one Season.

### Aim

***Finish the Season with the highest Fortune: Coin on hand plus five Coin for every Guild Seal you hold.***

### The Flow Of A Round

* **Rumor**: reveal a Rumor card; prices shift  
* **Permit Auction**: bid in secret for the right to travel and trade first  
* **Travel**: move your wagon along the road, paying Tolls  
* **Trade**: buy and sell cargo at the price track of the town you stand in  
* **Ledger**: settle contracts, pay wages, and check bandits

### Winning

* The Season ends after **round 8**.  
* Highest Fortune wins. The tiebreak is most Guild Seals, then most cargo cubes in the wagon.

### Falling Behind

* A house that cannot pay its wages is **Bankrupt** for that round and loses its Permit Tile.  
* A Bankrupt house still trades, but at Dust Season prices.

### Contracts

Contracts pay a bonus for delivering named goods to a named town. There are three kinds: ***Short Haul*** (due within two rounds), ***Long Haul*** (due by round 8), and ***Royal Order*** (paid only to the first house to deliver).

#### Example Contracts

* Deliver 3 Glass to Cinderford: 14 Coin and 1 Guild Seal (Short Haul)  
* Deliver 2 Silk and 1 Spice to Gullhaven: 30 Coin (Royal Order)

### Why Towns Matter

Each town buys and sells in its own way and charges its own toll. Some towns are friendly to certain goods, which is why the order of your route matters more than the speed of your wagon.

#### Tolls

* Toll Markers sit on a road segment after a Rumor closes the free path.  
* Pay the toll to the Guild bank when you cross.

#### Seals

Each Guild Seal is worth *five Coin* at the end and unlocks a *Guild Rank* privilege.

# Preparing The Table {#preparing}

## Seating And Starting Coin {#seating}

Houses sit around the table in any order. The oldest player holds the Dust Season Dial.

### Setup Steps

1. **Lay The Road**: Place the Road Board in the middle. Put the wagon meeples on **Ashgate**, the western end.  
2. **House Boards**: Give each house a House Board, a Bid Screen, and a wagon.  
3. **Starting Coin**: Each house takes **40 Coin** (two 20s). In a two-house game each house takes 50.  
4. **Cargo**: Fill the supply with cargo cubes by color and place one cube of each color on the matching price track at its **base** space.  
5. **Contracts**: Shuffle the Contract deck. Deal each house **three** and keep **two**; return the third to the bottom.  
6. **Guild Rank**: Each house takes the *Peddler* Guild Rank card.  
7. **Decks**: Shuffle the Rumor, Upgrade, and Bandit decks and place them face-down by the board.  
8. **Permits**: Set out as many Permit Tiles as there are houses plus one.  
9. **Dust Season Dial**: Set the Dial to **Calm**.  
10. **Round Tracker**: Place the round marker on round 1.  
11. **First Bidder**: The house whose wagon color is closest to white holds the First Bidder disc.

### Map Table

The number of towns in play depends on the number of houses. Use the table below.

| Town | 2 houses | 3-4 houses | 5 houses |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Ashgate | in play | in play | in play |
| Brine Wells | skip | in play | in play |
| Cinderford | in play | in play | in play |
| Dunmarket | skip | skip | in play |
| Emberly | in play | in play | in play |
| Fenmoor | skip | in play | in play |
| Gullhaven | in play | in play | in play |

*The road is ready\!*

For more on towns and prices, see the Towns and Goods sections. For a quick reminder of the five steps, see the Reference page.

#### Shorter Season

* **Three-round Season**: Play rounds 1 to 3 only; cut the Rumor deck to ten cards.  
* **Five-round Season**: Play rounds 1 to 5 only; cut the Rumor deck to fifteen cards.  
* The Fortune formula does not change.

# A Round Of Play {#round}

A round has five steps, always in the same order. Do each step completely before the next begins.

## Rumor Step {#rumor}

Turn over the top Rumor card. Read it aloud. Apply its effect to the Price Chart and any Toll Markers immediately. A Rumor with a duration stays on the table until that many rounds have passed.

On rounds 1 and 2 shuffle any **Embargo** Rumors out of the deck before drawing. Embargoes begin on round 3.

## Permit Auction {#auction}

Each house secretly places Coin behind its Bid Screen. Reveal together.

* The highest bid takes the first Permit Tile, the second highest takes the next, and so on.  
* Bids are paid to the bank, and a house that wins a Permit also takes the **Order Token** with the same number.  
* **Ties** are broken by Guild Rank, then by whoever is farther from Ashgate, then by the First Bidder disc.  
* A house may bid zero. It takes the last Permit Tile and acts last.

Permit order matters: it is the order in which houses travel and trade this round.

## Travel {#travel}

In Permit order, each house moves its wagon.

* A wagon may move up to its **Speed** (base 2) road segments.  
* Moving into a segment with a Toll Marker costs the toll shown, paid to the bank.  
* A wagon may stop in a town or on a road segment.  
* Two wagons may share a town. Two wagons on the same road segment trigger a **Standoff**: the house with the lower Permit number pays the other 2 Coin or turns back one segment.

## Trade {#trade}

A wagon that stands in a town may trade in that town. In Permit order, a house may:

* **Buy** any number of cargo cubes at the town's current price on the Price Chart.  
* **Sell** any number of cargo cubes it carries at the town's current price.  
* A wagon carries at most **6** cargo cubes (upgrades may raise this).  
* Buying a cube moves that good's price marker one step **up**. Selling a cube moves it one step **down**.  
* Each town will only buy goods marked on its Town card (see The Towns).

A house may not both buy and sell the same good in the same town in the same round.

## Ledger Step {#ledger}

1. **Contracts**: Each house may fulfill contracts it holds if its wagon stands in the named town and carries the named goods. Discard the cargo and take the reward.  
2. **Wages**: Pay **3 Coin** per upgrade card you own, to the bank. A house that cannot pay is Bankrupt this round.  
3. **Bandits**: If your wagon is on a road segment (not in a town), draw a Bandit card.  
4. **Dust Season**: Move the Dust Season Dial one step toward **Storm** on rounds 3 and 6.  
5. **Advance**: Move the round marker.

# The Towns {#towns}

Each town has a Town card listing what it buys, what it sells, and any special rule.

| Town | Specialty | Buys | Toll to enter |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Ashgate** | Mining town; the western end of the road | Salt, Glass | none |
| **Brine Wells** | Salt pans and brine ponds | Spice, Silk | 1 |
| **Cinderford** | Glassworks on a river of slag | Dye, Spice | 2 |
| **Dunmarket** | The great fair; all goods sell here | any | 3 |
| **Emberly** | Dye vats and ember kilns | Glass, Silk | 1 |
| **Fenmoor** | A marsh town, slow and cheap | Salt, Dye | none |
| **Gullhaven** | The sea gate; the eastern end of the road | Silk, Spice | 2 |

### Special Town Rules

* **Dunmarket**: The only town where a wagon may swap a Contract card for a new one (pay 3 Coin).  
* **Gullhaven**: Royal Orders are only delivered here.  
* **Ashgate**: A wagon starting a round in Ashgate may load one free Salt cube.

# Goods And Prices {#goods}

There are five goods: Salt, Dye, Glass, Spice, and Silk. Each has a price track on the Price Chart with seven spaces.

| Good | Base price | Dearest space | Cheapest space |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Salt | 2 | 6 | 1 |
| Dye | 3 | 8 | 1 |
| Glass | 4 | 9 | 2 |
| Spice | 6 | 12 | 3 |
| Silk | 8 | 15 | 4 |

### Glut And Shortage

When a price marker reaches its cheapest space, the good is in **Glut**: no town buys it for a round. When it reaches the dearest space, the good is in **Shortage**: the next sale of it pays double, after which the marker returns to base.

### Supply Limits

If the supply of a color of cargo cubes runs out, no one may buy that good until a cube is sold back.

# Contracts {#contracts}

Each house holds at most **three** contracts at once. Contracts are secret until fulfilled.

* **Short Haul**: due within two rounds of being taken; if missed, discard it and pay a **2 Coin** fee.  
* **Long Haul**: due by the end of round 8; no penalty if missed.  
* **Royal Order**: paid only to the first house to deliver; the Order is then discarded for everyone.

### Contract Card Reference

| Card | Kind | Delivery | Reward |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Glass for the Cinderford Guild | Short Haul | 3 Glass to Cinderford | 14 Coin, 1 Seal |
| The Fenmoor Salt Run | Short Haul | 4 Salt to Fenmoor | 8 Coin |
| Dye for Emberly | Long Haul | 2 Dye to Emberly | 10 Coin |
| Fair Day Spices | Long Haul | 3 Spice to Dunmarket | 18 Coin, 1 Seal |
| The Queen's Silks | Royal Order | 2 Silk, 1 Spice to Gullhaven | 30 Coin |
| The Admiral's Salt | Royal Order | 5 Salt to Gullhaven | 24 Coin, 1 Seal |

# Guild Ranks {#guild}

A house climbs Guild Ranks by collecting Guild Seals. Each rank gives a permanent privilege.

| Rank | Seals needed | Privilege |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |
| Peddler | 0 | None. Wagon Speed 2. |
| Trader | 1 | Win Permit ties. |
| Factor | 3 | Carry 1 extra cargo cube. |
| Syndic | 5 | Pay no tolls on the first road segment each round. |
| Magnate | 8 | Once per round, rebid after seeing the others. |

Rank is checked in the Ledger step. A house never loses a Rank.

# Caravan Upgrades {#upgrades}

At the start of the Trade step a house in a town with a market may buy **one** Upgrade card from the top three of the Upgrade deck. Upgrades cost wages (see the Ledger step).

| Upgrade | Cost | Effect |
| :---- | :---: | :---- |
| Iron-rimmed Wheels | 10 | Speed 3 instead of 2. |
| Second Wagon Bed | 14 | Carry 3 more cargo cubes (max 9). |
| Guild Letter | 8 | Ignore the first Embargo you meet. |
| Salt Lantern | 6 | Wagon is safe from bandits on the first road segment each round. |
| Factor's Seal Ring | 12 | Gain 1 Guild Seal immediately. |
| Mule Team | 9 | Ignore one Toll Marker per round. |
| Strongbox | 7 | When Bankrupt, keep your Permit Tile. |
| Dye Press | 11 | Sell Dye one price step higher than the chart shows. |

# Bandits And Escorts {#bandits}

When a wagon ends the Ledger step on a road segment, draw a Bandit card and resolve it.

* Bandit cards show a **Strength** from 1 to 6 and a **Demand**.  
* The house rolls an eight-sided die. If the roll is **equal to or greater than** the Strength, the wagon fights through.  
* If the roll is lower, the house must pay the Demand or lose cargo cubes of the owner's choice.  
* A house may hire an **Escort** before rolling: pay 3 Coin per +1 to the roll, up to +3.

### Bandit Demands

| Strength | Demand | Notes |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| 1-2 | 2 Coin | Rarely worth fighting. |
| 3-4 | 5 Coin or 1 cargo cube | |
| 5 | 8 Coin or 2 cargo cubes | Salt Lantern does not help. |
| 6 | The whole top cargo stack | The Crimson Band. |

### Escort Example

A house with 4 cargo cubes on a road segment draws a Strength 5 Bandit. It hires two Escorts for 6 Coin (+2 to the roll) and rolls a 3. The final result is 5, which equals the Strength, so the wagon fights through and keeps its cargo.

# Rumor Cards {#rumors}

Rumors are the main source of change on the Price Chart.

* **Festival at Dunmarket**: Spice and Silk each move up two steps. Lasts 1 round.  
* **Salt Glut**: Salt moves to its cheapest space. Lasts 2 rounds.  
* **Embargo on Brine Wells**: No wagon may enter Brine Wells. Place an Embargo Disc there. Lasts 2 rounds.  
* **Bridge Out**: Place a Toll Marker (3) on the segment between Cinderford and Dunmarket. Lasts 3 rounds.  
* **Dye Shortage**: Dye moves to its dearest space. Lasts 1 round.  
* **Quiet Roads**: No Bandit cards are drawn this round.  
* **Guild Audit**: Every house pays 1 Coin per Contract it holds.

### Rumor Severity

Early Rumors are mild. After round 4, the deck contains the harsher cards. If the Dust Season Dial reads **Storm**, apply every Rumor effect twice.

### Rumor Reference

| Rumor | Effect | Duration | Towns affected |
| :---- | :---- | :---: | :---- |
| Festival at Dunmarket | Spice, Silk up 2 | 1 | Dunmarket |
| Salt Glut | Salt to cheapest | 2 | All |
| Embargo on Brine Wells | No entry | 2 | Brine Wells |
| Bridge Out | Toll 3 on segment | 3 | Cinderford-Dunmarket |
| Dye Shortage | Dye to dearest | 1 | All |
| Quiet Roads | No bandits | 1 | All |
| Guild Audit | Pay 1 Coin per Contract | 1 | All |
| Storm Warning | Dial to Storm | - | All |

# End Of The Season {#end}

After the Ledger step of round 8 the Season is over. Score:

* Fortune \= Coin on hand \+ 5 per Guild Seal  
* Unfulfilled Long Haul contracts \= 0  
* Each leftover cargo cube is sold at the current price of its good in the nearest town

The house with the highest Fortune wins the title **Master of the Salt Road**.

# Reference {#reference}

The five steps of a round: Rumor, Permit Auction, Travel, Trade, Ledger.

### Frequently Asked

* **Can I bid more Coin than I have?** No. A bid is limited to the Coin on your side of the Bid Screen.  
* **Do I pay a toll to leave a town?** No, only to enter a segment with a Toll Marker.  
* **Does an Embargo block wagons already in the town?** No. They may stay but cannot trade.

### Solo Variant

A solo player runs one house against **the Ghost Wagon**: each round the Ghost Wagon takes the highest Permit, buys the cheapest good at its current town, and sells at the next. The solo player wins by finishing with a Fortune of 90 or more.
